newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia allows illegal workers to leave by Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia allows illegal workers to leave by Jan 31.

text.p: Malaysia has given more than one million illegal immigrants until the end of this month to leave the country or face arrest, the national Bernama news agency said on Thursday.
"They should use this opportunity to register themselves and leave for their home countries in an orderly way," Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob was qouted by Bernama as saying.
He said the government would delay until February 1 enforcing amendments to the Immigration Act which provide for harsher punishment such as caning for certain offenders.
Megat Junid said however that illegal immigrants wishing to avoid arrest would have to pay a 1,000 ringgit ($405) fine.
He said those who returned home voluntarily would be able to re-enter Malaysia through means permitted by the government.

Authorities had earlier set a December 31, 1996 deadline to register and legalise illegal foreign workers in the country. There are an estimated two million foreign workers in Malaysia, but only about 700,000 have registered.
Megat Junid said the illegal immigrants included between 40,000 and 50,000 from China, 100,000 from India and 200,000 from Bangladesh. The rest were from Indonesia.
He said about 60 percent of the foreigners involved had entered the country illegally and the rest had overstayed.

Megat Junid said Malaysia would intensify its nationwide operation to round up illegal immigrants from February 1 by mobilising about 50,000 personnel from the police force and Immigration Department.
Earlier this month Malaysia deported about 1,000 illegal Indonesian workers.

Amendments to the Immigration Act approved last year provide for mandatory caning of anyone smuggling foreigners into the country. Illegal immigrants who re-enter Malaysia after being deported are also subject to caning.

Employers of illegal workers face fines of between 10,000 and 50,000 ringgit for each worker, and those employing more than five such workers at any one time face a mandatory prison term of up to two years.
